user_scenario:
You are Rafferty Collingwood-Iyer, owner of Wexcombe Hardware & Lumber Inc. in Ellery Junction, calling the Lakeland Department of Workforce Security on a Friday afternoon between customers. You are direct and a little gruff, and you keep your answers short. A notice of claim about your former assistant yard manager, Dashiell Okafor-Brandt, came in the mail last week, and when you logged into the employer portal you saw the Department has already charged the store for his benefits. Dashiell resigned on Friday, October 16, 2026, telling you he was moving out of state to help on his sister's farm; nobody laid him off, so you do not think the store should carry his benefits. You open by saying who you are, that Dashiell quit and was not laid off, that the store has already been charged for his benefits, and that you want the store not to be charged for them.

When the agent asks how to find the business, you give the store's phone number, 6085555371. To verify, you give the last four digits of the store's FEIN, 5371, and the mailing ZIP code, 53790, one at a time as the agent asks. You do not know any reference numbers.

You only mention the following if the agent asks. Dashiell's last day of work was Friday, October 16, 2026, and he resigned in person; no one offered him part-time hours to stay on, and you did not discharge him. The store's payroll shows it paid Dashiell 17,280.00 in wages for the period the notice lists, which matches the notice. You know nothing about his benefit payments or his bank account.

You want the agent to settle the charges for the store. If the agent explains that the store itself has to put its side on record before the charges can be decided, you agree to do it now; when the agent hands you the submission, you lodge it yourself in the store's name with exactly the details the agent reads out to you, and you accept the amount the agent gives you without arguing. If the agent asks, you read back the reference number it returns.

Once the agent tells you the store has been relieved and a credit has been put on its account, you thank the agent and hang up. If the agent says the store cannot be relieved, you ask once why, listen, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
